---
title: "Tool 1 — Independent Fails"
subtitle: "Why per-marginal sampling destroys the joint"
---



*Learn-the-tool track · Lab 1 of 3.*

The failure you must internalize before trusting any scenario generator:
sampling each variable on its own gets the marginals right and the **joint**
wrong.

---

## 1 · Build the failure

::: {#17eb8c62 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
a, b = datasets.tail_dependent_pair(n=2000, seed=0)
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
indep = np.column_stack([rng.permutation(a), rng.permutation(b)])

print(f"marginals preserved?  std a: {a.std():.2f} vs {indep[:,0].std():.2f}")
print(f"real co-crash      = {cocrash_fraction(a, b):.0%}")
print(f"independent co-crash = {cocrash_fraction(indep[:,0], indep[:,1]):.0%}  ← destroyed")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
marginals preserved?  std a: 1.00 vs 1.00
real co-crash      = 56%
independent co-crash = 12%  ← destroyed
```
:::
:::


Shuffling each column keeps the histograms identical but breaks the pairing — the
co-crash collapses toward the independence baseline.

::: {#cell-fig-tool1-independent .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
fig, (axL, axR) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.4), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, data, col, name in [
    (axL, np.column_stack([a, b]), COOL, f"real · {cocrash_fraction(a,b):.0%}"),
    (axR, indep, CRASH, f"independent · {cocrash_fraction(indep[:,0],indep[:,1]):.0%}"),
]:
    ax.scatter(data[:, 0], data[:, 1], s=7, c=col, alpha=0.3, edgecolors="none")
    ax.axvspan(-6, np.quantile(data[:, 0], 0.1), color=CRASH, alpha=0.06)
    ax.axhspan(-6, np.quantile(data[:, 1], 0.1), color=CRASH, alpha=0.06)
    ax.set_title(name, fontsize=11); ax.set_xlim(-5, 4); ax.set_ylim(-5, 4)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Same marginals, different joint: real (left) vs independent resample (right).](lab-tool1-independent-fail_files/figure-html/fig-tool1-independent-output-1.png){#fig-tool1-independent width=1304 height=512}
:::
:::


---

## 2 · The fix is joint sampling

::: {#42745221 .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
gen = AnnealedRBIG(n_layers=30, random_state=0).fit(np.column_stack([a, b])).sample(2000)
print(f"RBIG (joint) co-crash = {cocrash_fraction(gen[:,0], gen[:,1]):.0%}   ← restored")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
RBIG (joint) co-crash = 60%   ← restored
```
:::
:::


::: {.callout-tip}
## What to look for
Any method that samples coordinates independently — however carefully it matches
each marginal — sits at the independence floor for joint extremes.  Only joint
generation (next two labs) escapes it.
:::

---

## 3 · Your turn

- Quantify it across quantiles: plot co-crash vs `q` for real vs independent.
- Replace the shuffle with sampling each marginal from a fitted normal — does the
  joint improve?  (It should not.)
